statements.venue: Official website, Artificial Intelligence issue page
statements.quote: It would also give the Department of Homeland Security Secretary, Commerce Sectary, and the Director of National Intelligence the authority to slow down or shutdown an AI system that can cause catastrophic harm.
statements.context: Her issue page describes her cosponsorship of the AI Kill Switch Act (H.R. 9917), which requires developers of the most powerful AI systems to keep the ability to throttle, suspend or shut them down.
statements.reason: In her own description of a bill she cosponsored, she names catastrophic harm from AI systems themselves, not limited to misuse; it is evidence of action rather than a direct statement of belief, so B/C boundary.

grade_reason: On her own 2026 AI issue page she describes advanced AI as posing catastrophic risk and an AI system that can cause catastrophic harm (not limited to misuse), and calls for a U.S.-China treaty to slow the AI race; no dismissive statements found. Both B statements are descriptions of actions (a bill and a letter), so a reviewer may prefer C.
notes: All 6 required web searches ran this time, plus 1 on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (7 total). None of them returned any page that mentions Escobar: the site: search returned only other house.gov domains, and the topic searches returned general coverage and other members (Casar, Khanna, Sanders, Ocasio-Cortez). So all statements come from her official AI issue page, which I re-downloaded on 2026-11-13 and checked that all three quotes still appear verbatim. The issue page has no date; 2026-09-17 is the earliest possible date, since it lists actions from 15-17 September 2026. Earlier run also opened her home page, press release list (latest 10, none on AI), the 17 Sep 2026 release (DocumentID=3364, Beyer letter, no quotes from her) and the 5 Oct 2026 Fort Bliss data center statement (no AI mention). Her issue page also lists the 15 Sep letter to Speaker Johnson (Liccardo release), the 16 Sep Beyer letter and the 18 Sep letter to Rubio and Bessent on U.S.-China talks; these are centrally handled multi-signer letters and are left out of the record, but her own one-line summary of the 15 Sep letter is included as a statement because it is her own wording. No source found showing she sponsored or co-sponsored the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538); search results list Casar as House sponsor and report about ten House Democrat cosponsors without naming her, but the congress.gov cosponsor list was not checked (congress.gov returned 403 in the earlier run), so this is not confirmed either way. The H.R. 9917 introduction date and her cosponsorship date could not be confirmed. No interviews, floor speeches or news reports quoting her on AI risk were found. The first quote keeps the page's typo 'Sectary'.
